title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: Copilot Cowork for GCC and GCC High
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, GCC licensing, access requirements and documented government differences are supported. Two admin paths stop on the correct settings page or section and should be extended to name the final control.

claims.claim: GCC access is admin-opt-in through a spending policy that includes Cowork.

claims.claim: The spending-policy path goes through Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > + Add spending policy > Policy scope > Identity > Specific groups > group > Select agents and services > Cowork.

The Model templates step appears only when you select Cowork in a spending policy.

claims.claim: POST /beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id}/serviceSettings adds a service setting to an existing spending policy.
claims.quote: Create a new spendingPolicyServiceSetting object to add a service to an existing spending policy. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/3f9e2c1a-0000-0000-0000-00000000c21b/serviceSettings

claims.claim: The service-setting request body requires serviceId and state.
claims.quote: Required properties are serviceId and state.

claims.claim: The cited service-setting creation reference uses another serviceId in its example and gives no Cowork value.
claims.quote: Searched: read spendingpolicyservicesetting-create in full for Cowork and serviceId. Its sole example uses researcherCritiqueAndCouncil; it supplies no Cowork serviceId. The separate spendingpolicy-create page does show cowork, but the claim is explicitly about this reference.

claims.claim: The Apps admin center path is Customization > Policy Management > Policy configurations > Create > Start with the basics > Choose the scope > Configure Settings.
claims.quote: Under Customization, select Policy Management. ... On the Policy configurations page, select Create. ... On the Start with the basics page ... On the Choose the scope page ... On the Configure Settings page, select the policies
claims.fix: Extend controls[1].ui.path to 'Customization > Policy Management > Policy configurations > Create > Start with the basics > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Allow web search in Copilot'. The existing path reaches the correct page; the policy name is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/manage-public-web-access.

claims.claim: POST /beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors creates a configuration monitor that can apply a baseline once.
claims.quote: Create a new configurationMonitor ... applies a desired-state baseline once in applyOnce mode. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors

claims.claim: The printed Graph automation uses beta APIs, with TCM capabilities in preview.
claims.quote: These capabilities are available in preview through Microsoft Graph beta.

claims.claim: Creating a monitor with mode applyOnce applies the desired-state baseline once rather than merely reading settings.
claims.quote: An active applyOnce monitor runs in the background on behalf of the signed-in administrator and then becomes inactive. Its result reports the outcome of the run.

claims.claim: The web-search resource is microsoft.copilot.allowwebsearch with resourceVersion 1 and properties.value.
claims.quote: "resourceType": "microsoft.copilot.allowwebsearch", "resourceVersion": 1, "properties": { "value": "0" }

claims.claim: Web-search properties.value of string 0 enables web search in Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: Controls web search. 0 enables it in Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: Web-search properties.value of string 1 disables web search in both Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: 1 disables it in both.

claims.claim: TCM supports these Copilot settings only in tenant-level policies and fails if the setting is configured in a group-level policy.
claims.quote: TCM supports these settings only in tenant-level policies in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center. ... If it is, monitoring, snapshots, remediation, and applyOnce fail for that resource.

claims.claim: Creating an applyOnce monitor supports delegated permissions only.
claims.quote: Creating an applyOnce monitor supports delegated permissions only.

claims.claim: AI Administrator is the signed-in user's required least-privileged role for web-search remediation and applyOnce.
claims.quote: For remediation and applyOnce, AI Administrator is the least-privileged Microsoft Entra role for the signed-in user. This role requirement applies to the user, not to the TCM service principal.

claims.claim: The TCM service principal needs delegated CopilotPolicySettings.ReadWrite for the web-search setting.
claims.quote: | microsoft.copilot.allowwebsearch | CopilotPolicySettings.ReadWrite | AI Administrator |

claims.claim: TCM is available only in the global service, not in national clouds.
claims.quote: TCM is available only in the global service, not in national clouds.

claims.claim: No API or PowerShell operation is documented for the tenant-level Cowork browser-access switch.
claims.quote: Searched: Cowork browser API policy; Cowork Local Browsing Allowed Graph; Cowork Allow browser access PowerShell; Cowork Browsing graph settings. Read cowork-local-browser, cowork-admin-governance and Edge CopilotCoworkToolActionsEnabled; no operation for this tenant switch.

claims.claim: The browser capability is disabled by default, including the GCC Local Browsing Allowed policy.
claims.quote: In GCC, local browsing is governed by the default-off Local Browsing Allowed policy. ... For worldwide and GCC tenants ... This feature is disabled by default.

claims.claim: The browser page inconsistently calls its path worldwide-only and applicable to worldwide and GCC tenants, while naming Local Browsing Allowed for GCC.
claims.quote: In GCC, local browsing is governed by the default-off Local Browsing Allowed policy. ... The web address and admin click path below describe the worldwide experience. ... For worldwide and GCC tenants, admins enable Cowork browsing by performing the following steps.

claims.claim: The spending-policy article says Auto-apply new services is selected by default.
claims.quote: By default, the Auto-apply new services toggle is selected for spending policies.

claims.claim: The GCC article does not say whether Auto-apply new services adds Cowork to existing GCC policies.
claims.quote: Searched: "Cowork" "GCC" "Auto-apply new services". Read cowork-government, cowork-access and usage-based-billing-manage-copilot-credits. The general article describes automatic additions; the GCC article does not address existing policies or this toggle.

claims.claim: The mixed licensing model reflects the required Microsoft 365 GCC Copilot license together with usage-based charges.
claims.quote: Cowork requires a Microsoft 365 GCC Copilot license, with no separate Cowork license. It is billed based on usage, so tenants pay only for what users actually use.
